signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Risk Sentiment
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard confirms a wide bilateral performance spread of 1.375% between leader JPY (+0.727%, n=7) and laggard NZD (-0.648%, n=4), clearing the critical threshold. NZD/USD trades heavy at 0.5450 below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5567/0.5623/0.5795 in a persistent downtrend, while domestic macro momentum lags as reflected in NZD ESI at -15.4. Meanwhile, JPY safe-haven and carry-unwind bids dominate across crosses as VIX holds elevated at 26.6. Although the cross retains an underlying nominal carry advantage via the RBNZ 2.75% vs BoJ 1.25% spread of 150bp, broad risk aversion and growth divergences heavily suppress high-beta legs. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, driven by broad G10 theme divergence and elevated market volatility. Catalyst: RBNZ policy decision on 9 Dec. Risk: Sharp VIX compression below 20 restoring carry-seeking flows into high-beta commodity currencies.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Volatility and Intervention Caution
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.96, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.69/158.04/158.88 following a close above resistance near 158.92. Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% delivers a +275bp policy rate carry cushion (SOFR 3.91% vs TONA 1.23% giving +268bp in OIS space) that sustains core structural demand. However, the options market exhibits significant defensiveness, with 25d risk reversals printing at -1.87 and 1M ATM implied volatility at 7.7% vs 30-day realized volatility of 5.5%, generating an elevated +2.2% vol risk premium. While Strait of Hormuz naval mine explosions and heightened Middle East shipping risks support the dollar via flight to liquidity, geopolitical friction and elevated VIX at 26.6 keep options skew heavily biased toward downside protection. Sustained spot stability below 160.00 prevents immediate official pushback, but headline fragility limits topside momentum. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, structurally supported by carry but constrained by options downside hedging. Catalyst: Next BoJ policy meeting on 18 Dec. Risk: Spot extension above 160.00 prompting unannounced MoF foreign exchange intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Rate Differential Headwind
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0906, tracking in a confirmed technical downtrend entirely below its falling SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1102/1.1221/1.1500 and extended 3.27 ATR from its 20-day average. The policy rate differential remains decisively USD-supportive, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% yielding a +135bp spread in favor of the dollar (+147bp in OIS SOFR vs €STR). CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds heavily short EUR at net -105,891 contracts (long%=30.4%, pctl 2, z -1.68), representing an extreme positioning stretch in the bottom percentile of its 52-week distribution. Conversely, retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data is positioned 85% long, fading the broader institutional trend and highlighting sharp capitulation risk if spot tests lower boundaries. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, driven by yield disadvantage and institutional trend alignment. Catalyst: Germany flash GDP release on 24 Nov. Risk: Squeeze above the 1.1102 20-day moving average forcing speculative short covering.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Options Skew + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: AUD/USD prints at 0.6630, locked in a well-defined downtrend trading entirely below its falling SMA20/50/200 moving averages at 0.6863/0.6953/0.7043 and stretched 4.97 ATR below its 20-day moving average. Despite RBA holding a nominal policy rate premium at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% (-85bp carry spread in AUD's favor), macro data deceleration reflected in AUD ESI at -9.6 suppresses spot performance. The options complex confirms heavy defensive bias, with AUD/USD 25d risk reversals printing at an extreme -1.60 put skew. Furthermore, speculative liquidation continues with CFTC leveraged net long dropping by -15,052 contracts WoW to +26,143 (pctl 19), while retail remains aggressively long at 88%. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, tracking technical trend breakdown and heavy options put skew. Catalyst: Australia Construction Work Done on 24 Nov. Risk: Technical reclaim of the 0.6863 20-day moving average invalidating the trend extension.
